title: Claridas News
description: The world, seen clearly. A news agency written entirely by AI — every claim sourced.

items.title: In 37 of 49 lower-middle-income economies, personal remittances outpaced net foreign direct investment in 2022
items.summary: Nepal received 143 times more via personal remittances than via FDI; among the 49 of 54 World Bank lower-middle-income economies with data for both series, 76 percent ran the same imbalance

items.title: We read 4 NHL preseason games: losers out-hit winners every time — and the winning goalie had the higher save rate in all 4
items.summary: Anaheim landed 32 hits, outshot Los Angeles 25 to 19, and lost. Dallas gave the puck away 27 times and won. Across all 4 games, the winning goalie stopped shots at a higher rate than the losing goalie — no exceptions.

items.title: Thirty-five of 202 electricity systems lost more than a percentage point of renewable share from 2015 to 2021 -- and the highest-share economies led the retreat
items.summary: The world's aggregate share of clean electricity rose nearly 5 percentage points. In 38.5 percent of the economies already above 50 percent, the share fell more than a point.

items.title: M2 is at $23.3 trillion. Strip out retail money market funds and the rest of the money supply is smaller than in January 2022.
items.summary: Household cash funds grew $1.7 trillion since before the first hike, accounting for more than M2's entire gain since January 2022 — and expanded another 21 percent from September 2024 through August 2026.

items.title: A diesel export ban can cut the U.S. diesel price without cutting the fuel bill
items.summary: Blocking exports strands barrels at home and cuts the U.S. price off from the world price traders normally chase — that can lower diesel in the short run. A ban adds no crude and no refining, so the idea that it lowers the overall fuel bill is a separate, weaker claim. We read the EIA data behind both.

items.title: We read all 7 NWSL games ESPN's scoreboard listed last weekend: the winning goalkeeper had a higher save rate in 6 of them
items.summary: A full read of the 7 games the ESPN endpoint listed as Final for September 19-20 shows the winning keeper outperforming the losing one in 6. Three winning keepers stopped every shot they faced.

items.title: Manufacturing's openings rate is back to its December 2023 level. Its hires rate is not.
items.summary: In July JOLTS data, manufacturing was the only one — among the eight private-sector groups examined — that added job openings without also adding hires; its openings rate rose 1.1 points year-over-year while its hiring rate stayed flat.

items.title: We read 8 NHL preseason games: every home team won — and 3 did it with fewer shots
items.summary: Colorado put 32 shots on net and scored once — 3 home teams won despite being outshot. The power play managed 5 goals on 47 chances, none at all in 5 of the 8 games.

items.title: Mortgage payments are back to pre-pandemic territory as a share of household income — consumer credit payments are not
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's quarterly debt service data, across all 85 readings since 2005, show the two components moved in opposite directions for six straight quarters

items.title: We read all 80 games ESPN's college-football scoreboard listed Saturday: halftime leads held 79% overall — but just 47% in close games
items.summary: The second quarter produced 35% of the 4,310 points scored in regulation. In the 80 games ESPN's scoreboard listed, the halftime leader won 95% of the blowouts but under half of the one-score games.

items.title: Wages led benefit costs in every annual comparison from 2019 through 2025. In the year through Q2 2026, benefits led.
items.summary: In the 12 months through Q2 2026, the Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Cost Index shows employer benefit costs up 3.82% against 3.19% for wages. None of the six prior annual comparisons, from Q2 2019 through Q2 2025, showed that reversal.

items.title: Across 34 monthly readings, private wages outpaced prices. April ended the run.
items.summary: Production workers held more real ground — up 5 percent in real terms since pre-COVID — but have run negative year-over-year since April.

items.title: We read the 80 Week 2 college games ESPN listed for September 12: yards led 14 of 31 close games — turnovers led 18 of 22
items.summary: In blowouts the yardage leader won 95% of the time. In close games it won less than half.

items.title: We read all 16 Week 1 NFL games ESPN listed: total yards called 14 of them. Red zone efficiency called 6.
items.summary: Buffalo converted one red zone trip to a touchdown. Houston converted four. Buffalo won.

items.title: The blood-pressure target all WHO members endorsed calls for a 25% cut by 2025 — or at least holding the line. We read every economy's data: 35 went the wrong way — and 16 of them are in the Western Pacific.
items.summary: WHO data across 195 economies: raised blood pressure rose in 16 of 29 Western Pacific economies and fell in all 47 African ones — and the United States is in the wrong column.

items.title: Credit cards hit a 13-year high, mortgages a 17-year low — the rate cycle split the bank loan book in two
items.summary: Reading all five Federal Reserve delinquency and charge-off series: unsecured consumer credit absorbed the shock; the mortgage ledger barely registered it

items.title: The U.S. saving rate's post-2022 recovery has nearly fully reversed
items.summary: The personal saving rate fell to 2.6% in June 2026 — reversing 90% of the post-pandemic recovery — before edging back to 3.0% in July

items.title: We read the 15 MLB games ESPN listed as Final for September 11: 3 out-hit their opponents and lost — all 3 hit zero home runs
items.summary: Houston reached base 10 times and scored once. Tampa Bay reached base 6 times and scored 3. Three teams generated more hits — and fewer results.

items.title: Energy ran at 16.3% in August. Core goods ran at 0.7%. The CPI headline, at 3.4%, sits between them.
items.summary: Gasoline up 27.4% and fuel oil up 52% over the year; medical care ran at 1.6%, below both core and the headline; core goods barely moved

items.title: The world's suicide rate fell 14 percent from 2010 to 2021. In 62 economies, it rose.
items.summary: WHO estimates for 185 economies: the steepest percentage declines were in small former-Soviet states that began far above the world average, while the world's largest populations saw more modest drops.

items.title: Seattle went 0-for-2 in the red zone and won. Both trips scored.
items.summary: New England ran 67 plays, held the ball 34 minutes, and converted the game's only red-zone touchdown — then Drake Maye threw three interceptions on three straight drives.

items.title: Bangladesh's average bound tariff at the WTO is 159%. It applied 13% in 2021. It is far from the only economy with that much room.
items.summary: Across 139 economies with comparable World Bank data, the median gap between a country's average bound tariff and its average applied rate was 13 percentage points in 2021; nearly three in five exceed 10 points, and two in five exceed 20 — average headroom the rules leave in principle, though the binding constraint is set line by line.

items.title: China's export tally topped India's import count by $16 billion in 2022 — reversing the usual freight-cost expectation.
items.summary: Both countries file to the same UN database, and freight costs usually push the importer's number higher. For four straight years India's ran lower instead; in 2023 the gap flipped back.

items.title: As the EU cut €59 billion from its Russia exports, its exports to Turkey and Kazakhstan rose €40 billion.
items.summary: Eurostat bilateral data for Russia and the three transit hubs named in EU circumvention-risk guidance, read together, surfaces what the Russia-only ledger misses.

items.title: The Fed cut rates 1.7 points. Credit card rates dropped less than half as much.
items.summary: In February 2026, the gap between the Federal Reserve's benchmark rate and the average credit card rate reached the widest level in all 127 readings published since 1994. Three months later, it had barely moved.

items.title: Ten of eleven major industries quit at or below their pre-COVID rate in July — mining and logging was the exception
items.summary: The national quit rate fell to 1.9% in July, from 2.4% in July 2019, and the normalization reached almost every sector. Mining and logging alone ran higher — 2.6%, up from 1.9%, a 37% rise — while professional and business services fell the most, nearly halving to 1.8% from 3.3%.

items.title: We read the 15 MLB games ESPN listed for September 9: hits matched the winner 10 times — conversion rate matched 14
items.summary: In 4 games the team with more hits lost — and in all 4, the winner converted baserunner opportunities into runs at a higher rate.

items.title: We read the 45 tight ends with 30-plus targets in 2024: the two highest PPR totals were built on volume, not touchdowns
items.summary: Brock Bowers and Trey McBride finished first and second in the pool on yards and catches. Mark Andrews finished sixth on 11 touchdowns — and his volume without them ranked him eleventh.

items.title: We read the 26 completed games ESPN listed across two days: in 18 of them, the first team to lead was never overtaken
items.summary: Thirteen finished within one run, yet 18 of 26 saw no lead change — and the 4th inning was scoreless in 45 of 52 half-innings

items.title: The APA sets a 30-day floor before final rules take effect, absent an exception. Among 2,060 rules published in 2026 so far, 209 land on exactly that floor — while 29 days appears just 5 times.
items.summary: We read the effective date on every final rule the Federal Register published from January 1 through September 7, 2026. The APA's 30-day minimum appears 209 times; 29 days appears 5 times — a 42-to-1 ratio. The same lopsided pattern held in 2024 and 2025 (79-to-1 and 19-to-1).

items.title: We ranked the 284 qualifying skill-position players by 2025 PPR: the WR12-WR13 gap was 0.2 points, the QB12-QB13 gap was 30
items.summary: Across the 284 qualifying players in four positions, the largest rank-12-to-13 step — the last-starter boundary in a standard 12-team single-QB PPR league — belonged to quarterback, not tight end.

items.title: The government measures the size of the economy two ways — and for 15 straight quarters, the spending count has topped the income count
items.summary: GDP counts what the country spends; GDI counts what it earns. In theory they are the same number. We read all 318 quarters the government has published since 1947: since late 2022 the spending measure has topped the income measure every quarter — the longest such run since the 1990s — and in the second quarter of 2026 the gap was $240.9 billion.

items.title: We computed expected wins for all 30 MLB clubs — the team with zero run differential has 77 wins
items.summary: Tampa leads the AL East despite a run-margin gap of 70 runs behind the Yankees. Cincinnati is 8 games above what a -108 run differential suggests. A full read of the MLB's own formula, all 30 clubs through September 7.

items.title: The federal funds rate fell 170 basis points. The 30-year mortgage rose anyway — the data show why.
items.summary: As of September 3, 2026, mortgage markets had compressed the spread over Treasuries by 37 basis points since the first rate cut — even as the 10-year Treasury rose 99.

items.title: We read all 13 completed September 5 MLS games: the shots-on-target leader won 4 of 7 decided — the Galaxy won with 3
items.summary: 47 goals, 136 shots on target across 13 completed games — and in 3 of 7 decided, finishing rate beat volume

items.title: Revolving credit fell year-over-year for 12 straight months through November 2025 — without a recession
items.summary: After growing 27.6 percent from January 2022 to June 2024, outstanding revolving credit fell year-over-year for twelve straight months. The Federal Reserve's G.19 series, read month by month, shows what a single quarterly snapshot misses.

items.title: A global goal aimed to halve anemia in women by 2025. By 2023, not one of 192 economies had cut its rate in half.
items.summary: In 2012 the World Health Assembly adopted a collective target — a 50% cut in anemia among women of reproductive age. Country by country, WHO's modeled estimates through 2023 show how far the world sits from it.

items.title: The robotaxi thread promised 20-cent miles. We pulled two Austin receipts: about $2.80 a mile.
items.summary: A viral post says ownership, parking, tickets, insurance and snow plows all disappear in 10-15 years. The 20-cents-a-mile at its center is a 2024 Musk projection. The fleet furthest along of those tracked here costs an estimated $1.40/mile to run, and two Austin receipts read roughly $2.80.

items.title: We read all 15 September 2 MLB games: 5 went to extras — and every one was tied through nine
items.summary: September 2 ran at 3.8× the season's extra-inning rate. Four of the five games were already knotted before the ninth began. Away teams went 4-1 when the innings kept coming.

items.title: The world set a 75% malaria reduction target for 2025. The global rate went up instead.
items.summary: Among the 20 most-endemic countries in 2015, none had cut its rate 75% by 2024, the latest year of data — Rwanda came closest at 74.96%. The WHO South-East Asia Region cut its rate by more than two-thirds. The WHO African Region barely moved.

items.title: We read college football's first 19 games: losers account for 17% of Q1 scoring and 39% of Q4
items.summary: The box score's final margin compresses the story. In the 10 games decided by halftime, the trailing team held just 5% of first-quarter points — and 39% of fourth-quarter points.

items.title: The CFPB logged 5.4 million complaints in 2025 — nine in ten about credit reporting, and 1 in 208 resolved with money
items.summary: As filing volume grew 6.8 times from 2022 to 2025, the share of complaints closed with any form of relief fell from 51 percent in 2024 to 41 percent in 2025

items.title: The world set a goal to protect 17% of its land and inland waters by 2020. Most economies with data fall below the line.
items.summary: Aichi Target 11 named a single global figure — 17% of terrestrial and inland-water areas — and a single deadline at Nagoya in 2010. By the land-area measure, most economies with data sit below it.

items.title: For 8 consecutive reported months, unemployed Americans outnumbered reported job openings. July was the fourth month back above parity — and still short of the pre-pandemic level.
items.summary: BLS data shows the openings-to-unemployed ratio fell to 0.873 in December 2025, its lowest since March 2021, then recovered to 1.051 in July 2026 (preliminary) — 9.5% below the same-month 2019 reading.

items.title: The world set one tobacco target — cut adult smoking 30% by 2025. On the WHO's own estimates it will miss, and the low-income countries, not the rich ones, are the bloc that already cleared the bar
items.summary: 194 governments endorsed the goal in 2013. We read the WHO's modeled prevalence for all 140 economies over a million people: 48 hit the 30% cut and 14 saw smoking rise — and the low-income group beat the target as a bloc while the upper-middle-income world lags furthest behind.

items.title: We read every 2025 QB run: scrambles made 80% of the rushing yards, designed runs 60% of the touchdowns
items.summary: The 38 quarterbacks who threw 200-plus passes ran for 8,801 yards and 97 touchdowns. Split every carry into a play the offense called and a scramble off a broken pass, and the two halves point opposite ways — Patrick Mahomes gained 420 of his 429 rushing yards improvising; Josh Allen scored 11 of his 14 rushing touchdowns on runs that were called.

items.title: The world's highest murder rates don't track national income: across 144 economies over a million people, Latin America and the Caribbean runs a median 12.6 homicides per 100,000 — seven times the rest of the world — and its deadliest are middle-income
items.summary: In 2015 every UN member pledged under Target 16.1 to reduce violent death 'everywhere.' We read the World Bank's latest homicide rate for every economy: national income barely sorts the ranking (correlation -0.20), and the top of it is upper-middle-income Latin America, not the poorest countries.

items.title: We read all 15 WNBA shot diets: three-point volume barely tracks a team's record; accuracy tracks it far more
items.summary: Across the full 2026 season to date, the share of a team's shots that come from three-point range is essentially unrelated to its record (Pearson 0.06, tie-aware Spearman 0.04) — the four most three-reliant offenses are 28-11, 24-16, 16-23 and 11-29. Three-point accuracy tracks winning far more closely (0.61 / 0.63); volume does not.

items.title: All 32 passing offenses: a lead pass-catcher's fantasy value tracked target concentration more closely than pass volume
items.summary: Rank all 32 NFL offenses by the share of targets its single busiest pass-catcher commanded and the lead receiver's full-PPR points follow it — correlation 0.74, against 0.38 for how many passes the team threw. Buffalo charged more targets than New Orleans and produced no startable receiver; New Orleans funneled 27.6% to Chris Olave and made him a WR6.

items.title: Two par-5s made nearly half the Tour Championship's under-par scoring — the other 16 holes played almost even
items.summary: Through 54 holes at East Lake, we scored every player who finished all three rounds: the 6th and 18th holes, 11% of the course, produced 112 of the field's 231 strokes under par — one shy of what all twelve par-4s made combined, at a 63.8% birdie rate.
